html:
Tash Rabat is a stone caravanserai high in the Tian Shan mountains of Kyrgyzstan, near the pass to Kashgar, usually dated to the 15th century.

It stands at about 3,500 metres in a remote valley, a low building of rough stone under a central dome, with some thirty rooms. Some scholars think an older Christian or Buddhist monastery stood on the site before. Merchants and travellers on the Silk Road between the Fergana valley and Kashgar in the Tarim Basin sheltered there from snow and raiders.

Its walls survived because few people lived nearby to take the stones. Restored in Soviet times, it is now one of the best known sights of Kyrgyzstan, and herders still pitch yurts in the valley beside it in summer.
sum: Tash Rabat is a stone caravanserai high in the Tian Shan mountains of Kyrgyzstan, near the pass to Kashgar, usually dated to the 15th century.
